title: NEON ground beetle catches in 46 US sites in 2014-2023 had no clear national decline; hot previous summers and dry years lowered catches each year, but drying did not explain site trends
abstract: Question: Did ground beetle (Carabidae) pitfall catches at NEON sites decrease in 2014-2023, and does multi-year drought explain the change, as a 24-year German forest record reported (71% decrease with a six-year SPEI drought)? Approach: We used 103,310 trap samples and 242,795 carabids at 46 sites (NEON RELEASE-2026 via neonDivData) and Daymet weather. Per-site Poisson models controlled trap identity, season coverage and the 2018 and 2023 protocol cuts. A written plan specified the trend and drought tests before the weather fits. Results: The pooled trend was -1.8% per year (95% CI -4.6 to +1.0; 42 sites). A balanced 2016-2023 panel gave +0.9% (-2.7 to +4.7). The protocol cuts caused no index step. Each 1 C of warmth during trapping raised catches by 2.8% (1.0 to 4.7). The pre-specified six-year water balance term was +0.002 log units per SD (-0.064 to +0.068). Sites that became drier did not lose more beetles. The German decline implies about 0.44-0.51 per SD; all NEON estimates exclude it. Post hoc first-difference models with year effects showed that a hot previous summer lowered catches by 10% per 1 C (site-permutation p = 0.006) and that a wet year raised them by 9% per SD (p = 0.004). Signs repeated in east, west, forest, open, both periods and three index variants. Limitations: Pitfall catches measure activity-density. Most NEON sites became wetter in 2014-2023, so severe drought exposure was rare. The year-to-year weather models are post hoc. The data are a curated copy that we could not audit against NEON tables. The German scaling uses our approximate index. The study has no species-trait test and no air-pollution test.

citations.reason: Weiss, von Wehrden and Linde (2024): carabid decline after six-year drought in a German forest. We test its generality across NEON sites; NEON drought sensitivity is at least 2 times smaller than the implied German rate.
Kaspari et al. (2022): no 5-year activity-density trend in NEON pitfall bycatch. We extend to 10 years of carabid counts with protocol-cut control.
Earlier NEON study in this campaign (mosquitoes and heat); same neonDivData access route after NEON API HTTP 403. No data or code reused.
Warm nights raised UK moth trap catches; we find the pitfall equivalent (2.8% per 1 C of trap-interval warmth).
